chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman, is there upon her an Adhan and an Iqamah? He said: No.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah: A title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.إِقَامَةٌ: Iqamah: The call to establish the prayer

ai.seo_question: Do women have to say Adhan and Iqamah in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) confirms the exemption of women from reciting the Adhan and Iqamah, reflecting the Shia juristic view that these calls are acts of public proclamation (*ijab*) primarily associated with men. This ruling underscores the distinction in Shia fiqh between obligatory public duties and private worship, where women's prayer validity does not depend on these specific vocalizations.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzān, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the woman, ‘Is there a recitation of an Azān and an Iqamah upon her?’ Heasws said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 18. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if a woman is required to say Adhan and ‘Iqamah. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, she is not required.’”
